articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for the Wideband Modeling of a 10 kVA Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper aims to model a 10 kVA power transformer used in electrical distribution networks in rural areas in Brazil, with the goal of enabling the study of communication data transmission in smart grids through the power distribution infrastructure — the Power Line Communication (PLC) technology. This study is essential to ensure the feasibility of using this technology, considering that transformers exhibit variable characteristics with frequency and can affect the quality of signal transfer via PLC. In this context, the paper seeks to introduce a new approach to the black-box modeling of power transformers, replacing the need for frequency sweep tests, which require extensive point-by-point measurements, with a single impulse test capable of exciting the entire frequency range necessary for determining the elements of the transformer model. To validate the model, a voltage step, that excites the entire frequency band of interest, is applied.

articleTitle: An RC model to represent the voltage profile of a second-life lithium-ion battery
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper evaluated a first-order equivalent circuit model to represent the voltage profile of a second-life lithium-ion battery sourced from an electric vehicle. Experimental tests were conducted to build look-up tables for the battery and construct the model using the least squares method to fit the simulated and experimental operating curves. The model was validated based on a real battery operating curve. The battery tests were carried out in a controlled environment to avoid the influence of external factors. The mean absolute percentage error in the voltage magnitude divergence between the experimental and simulated curves was 0.676%. The results were also extended to a second-order model; however, the mean absolute percentage error for the second-order model was 0.861%.

articleTitle: On Evaluating Series Capacitor Bank Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper deals with the evaluation of series capacitor bank protection applied to transmission lines. To do so, a series-compensated double-circuit transmission line, modeled in Alternative Transients Program (ATP), was evaluated by means of sensitivity and transient analyses. The results reveal how series-capacitor bank protection can bypass the capacitor banks under some fault scenarios, in such a way that this dynamic behavior must be accounted by protection engineers when setting relay parameters.

articleTitle: Evaluating Incremental-Quantity Protection Elements in Hybrid Transmission Lines with Overhead and Underground Segments
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of incremental-quantity protection elements TD32 and TD21 in hybrid transmission lines (HTLs) that combine overhead transmission lines (OHLs) and underground cables (UGCs). Ground faults were simulated using a 380 kV/60 Hz power system in PSCAD, with six configurations and 216 fault scenarios per configuration under varying conditions, including fault time, location, resistance, and phase. Analysis through scatter and boxplot plots revealed significant differences in the operation times of protection functions between HTLs and OHLs, impacting overall system reliability. Specifically, the presence of UGCs alters fault detection times (Start Logic) and the performance of protective relays regarding incremental quantities, potentially leading to delays in fault clearance. These findings underscore the necessity for protective schemes to accommodate the unique dynamics of HTLs, enhancing overall system reliability and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Methodology for Assessing Induced Currents in Cable Sheaths: Comparative Analysis of Sectionalized and Continuous Cross-Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for calculating induced currents in sectionalized and continuous cross-bonding systems of high-voltage cables, offering an alternative to the correction factor suggested by the IEC 60287 standard. Unlike the simplified approach in the standard, the proposed methodology provides physically robust results by considering parameters and variables often neglected by the correction factor. This allows for a more accurate evaluation of energy losses, cable ampacity, and operating temperatures under various conditions. The methodology enhances the accuracy of the analysis, offering valuable insights for improving system performance, reliability, and safety while addressing the complexities associated with cross-bonding configurations.

articleTitle: A generalized FEM-based framework for earth return impedance calculations on vertically-multilayered media
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Accurate modeling of earth return impedance is essential for assessing electromagnetic interference (EMI) in pipelines near overhead transmission lines (OHL). Conventional models, limited by assumptions of homogeneous or horizontally stratified soils, often subestimate EMI risks. This paper introduces a finite element method (FEM)-based approach to calculate self and mutual impedances in vertically stratified soils, overcoming limitations of analytical models. Compared with homogeneous cases, the FEM approach demonstrates improved accuracy, with impedance values reflecting real soil complexities. A case study with a 150 kV OHL near an underground pipeline highlights the efficacy of the proposed framework in capturing EMI effects in complex soil environments.

articleTitle: Optimizing Static Antenna Arrays for Constant Power Levels in Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Classical methods of designing an array, in general, are useful to project uniform arrays varying only their input magnitude and phase. This work proposes a design process of a static antenna array with the antennas physically steered and in any 3D position while also considering a target satellite to communicate with. This introduces more degrees of freedom to the problem when compared to more classical approaches.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Analysis on Integrated Access and Backhaul Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) networks leverage key characteristics of 5th generation networks, providing high-quality and reliable connections. This is achieved by efficiently utilizing the newly available millimeter wave (mmWave) spectrum for backhaul, leading to easier implementation and lower costs compared to other solutions. However, these improvements come with an associated energy consumption cost, which must be carefully considered in network planning to ensure sustainability. To assess the impact of transmit power on quality of service (QoS) and network planning, base station deployment optimization is performed for an IAB-enabled network, considering different transmit power values for both macro base station and small base station. The results indicate that reducing transmit power does not necessarily lead to a decrease in QoS. Although coverage is negatively impacted, the trade-off between coverage and energy efficiency strongly favors solutions with lower energy consumption.

articleTitle: An Instrumentation System for a Laboratory-Scale Wind Generation Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental evaluation of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) under various disturbances, including wind gusts, turbulence, and load variations, aiming to investigate their effects on the generator’s voltage, current, and vibration. To perform the analysis, an instrumentation system and a monitoring interface were developed to oversee and control the experimental test bench. Additionally, a motor speed control system was implemented to simulate different wind profiles acting on the generator. The results clearly highlight the impact of these disturbances on generation stability and efficiency, with particular emphasis on voltage, current, and vibration.

articleTitle: High-Gain Broadband Printed Antenna for W-Band Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)

authors.preferredName: Lucas Dos Santos Barros De Sousa

abstract: This article presents the design of a printed antenna for automotive radar applications, operating in the W band from 75.5 GHz to 85.5 GHz. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 9.5 dB and maintains a high radiation efficiency above 85% across the band. Its compact design and printed configuration enable integration into modern automotive radar systems, providing a cost-effective solution with reliable performance in high-frequency environments. The simulation results confirm the high efficiency and functioning of the project, with the prospect of additional steps planned for manufacturing and testing

articleTitle: OpenDER Model: Assessing IEEE Std 1547-2018 Voltage/Power Control Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper evaluates the OpenDER model’s performance in simulating inverter-based distributed energy resources (DERs) using IEEE Std 1547-2018 control modes. Integrated with OpenDSS via Python, the OpenDER model is assessed under Constant Power Factor, Volt-VAr, Watt-VAr, Constant Reactive Power, and Volt-Watt modes. Results reveal the model’s effectiveness in maintaining power factor and adjusting reactive power. The results demonstrate the model’s effectiveness in following the control curves proposed by IEEE Std 1547-2018, with only minor deviations in some cases, such as the Volt-VAR curve. Additionally, the differences between Categories A and B are highlighted for the same operating mode, which, in turn, affects the feeder voltage at the DER connection node. The dynamic DER response to voltage deviations is also presented, showing its ability to transition between Mandatory and Continuous Operation modes. The findings highlight the model’s strengths and areas for improvement, offering insights for better DER integration in power systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Behavior of Digital Protections of Transmission Lines When Subjected to Frequencies Outside the Operating Range, in a Real Case
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper reports on the improper operation of the overvoltage protection, in a real case, due to the estimation error of its phasors, when the frequency of the voltage signal was not compatible with the sampling frequency. It was possible to observe the recovery time of the frequency tracking signal. The results obtained by applying the simulation of the occurrence in the IED are also illustrated, as well as an analysis of the concepts applied in the calculations of the IED phasors. Thus, the conclusion is presented by exposing the solution adopted for the referred problem.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of J. Martí and Universal Line Models for Pipeline Coupling Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper evaluates the J. Martí and Universal Line Model (ULM) for transient EMI responses between a transmission line and a pipeline. A simulation tool models frequency-dependent series impedance (Z) and shunt admittance (Y) using high-frequency EMI-specific formulas, with results compared to ATPDraw simulations. Findings indicate that accurate high-frequency induced voltages require these formulations and that the ULM model offers the best accuracy for representing EMI effects.

articleTitle: A Base Station Deployment Optimization using Energy Efficiency for Networks with Integrated Access and Backhaul
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) networks are a technology proposed in recent 3rd generation partnership project releases for 5th generation (5G)-new radio (NR) networks due to their potential to reduce deployment and backhauling costs, as well as to improve spectrum usage. In 5G networks (IAB ones included), it is necessary to solve the base station deployment problem for the installation and expansion of the network while ensuring good service quality. In this work, we optimize the positioning of base stations (BSs) using genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) having energy efficiency (EE) as the optimization metric. Different scenarios are considered, and the obtained results show that GA outperforms PSO in all the studied cases. The solutions found by the algorithms are analyzed using Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate mean EE and Signal to interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) as key performance indicators, which suggest that a joint optimization could be carried out as to obtain a network with high communication quality and good EE.

articleTitle: Analysis of Meteorological Variables Used for Solar Power Generation Forecast
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: As photovoltaic solar energy depends on meteorological variables such as irradiance, air temperature and wind speed, they are used in artificial intelligence models to carry out generation forecasts. However, it is necessary to evaluate the quality of the data and its relationship with the target variable for prediction to find the best data source to be used in model training. This work aims to graphically and statistically evaluate four sources of meteorological data. Using Pearson and Spearman correlation and scatter plots to understand the behavior of irradiance, air temperature and wind speed with photovoltaic solar generation in relation to the active power at the inverter output. In the end, there are valuable insights into the variables and data sources analyzed, being a step prior to modeling the forecast of solar photovoltaic generation.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in a Multiterminal HVDC Transmission System Using Discrete Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this paper, a study of fault detection and classification in HVDC transmission lines, using the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) is present. The High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission lines allow a large amount of energy generation in several locations to be supplied to distant points in the electrical system where there is a high demand for power. This need can be met with the use of multiterminal HVDC (MTDC) systems. Due to the high fault currents that can be reached in these MTDC systems, effective protection schemes with fast action and selectivity are necessary. For this purpose, the analyses are developed through simulation in Matlab/Simulink, and it is attested that with the algorithm proposed in the detection and classification analysis, respectively, the protection is quickly ensured with 98.07% accuracy, and it allows the identification of 100% of the poles involved in the faults.

articleTitle: Lightning Response on Cable Core and Sheath in Single-Circuit Underground Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Throughout their operational lifespan, underground cables (UGCs) encounter diverse transient phenomena, with lightning strikes being of notable concern, particularly for hybrid cable-overhead lines . Lightning impulses wield significant influence, particularly at the termination section where the underground line meets the overhead line. This study investigates the effects of lightning strikes on both the cable sheaths and the core. The study evaluates the impact of generalized formulations developed by Xue and simplified formulations developed by Pollaczek for line parameter calculations. Furthermore, the study considers the inclusion of soil parameters dependent on frequency. Two scenarios are examined: a theoretical scenario where sheaths are presumed disconnected from the ground and a more realistic scenario where sheaths are short-circuited and grounded. The results indicate that in the theoretical scenario, the percentage deviation reaches 110.7% in the cable core of phase B. Conversely, in the more realistic scenario, a maximum percentage deviation of 68.4% is observed in the sheaths when utilizing the Pollaczek formulation.

articleTitle: Electric Field Analysis and Optimization Applied to the Design of a High Voltage Test Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper proposes the development of a high-voltage transformer for dielectric tests, designed to minimize the electric field in critical regions, such as the ends of the windings, aiming to reduce stress on the insulation and prolong the equipment's service life. To achieve this, three optimization geometrical strategies (trapezoidal, exponential, and quadratic) were applied, based on mathematical equations and computational simulations using the finite element method. The two-dimensional transformer design included adjustments in the arrangement of winding layers and the use of weighted parameters to improve the electric field profile. Simulations showed that the quadratic optimization redistributed the electric field more efficiently, with a 6.82% decrease.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Penetration Loss for Building Materials in 5G FR1 Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This article presents a measurement analysis of propagation loss in materials at the 3.5 GHz frequency applied to 5G FR1 networks. The analysis is based on an advanced 5G network using a Test Station equipment and the experiment is carried out in a controlled environment using an anechoic chamber. The loss due to the materials are obtained from the difference in the intensity of the Reference Signal Receive Power (RSRP), which is observed in the user’s equipment (UE) without obstructions (free space and LoS) and with obstructions (different materials and NLoS). Finally, the loss values obtained for the different materials studied are presented, as well as how each building material can influence the scheduling of the 5G network.

articleTitle: Measuring Public Wi-Fi Security Awareness via Captive Portal Connections Using a Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This article proposes the implementation of a captive portal system on a microcontroller to assess users’ maturity regarding the safe use of public Wi-Fi networks. The use of public Wi-Fi networks has become increasingly common in places like cafes, airports, shopping centers, and hotels. However, many users are unaware of the risks associated with using these unsecured networks, such as personal information theft, privacy invasion, and cyberattacks. This study aims to utilize a microcontroller to generate a signal mimicking a known public network, where, upon user login, an educational authentication portal will be displayed. This portal will not only provide information about security risks but also evaluate the users’ maturity level in adopting safe practices on public Wi-Fi networks, offering guidelines on how to protect their data and devices.

articleTitle: Parabolic Antenna Array Position Estimation and Calibration Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Steerable arrays of small parabolic antennas are more cost-effective than large steerable parabolic dishes. However, installation and aging can introduce array parameter errors, such as positioning inaccuracies and variations in amplitude and phase. To mitigate these non-idealities, array calibration is performed. In this work, position calibration is followed by amplitude and phase calibration, evaluated under both biased and unbiased error conditions in benchmarking tests. Results demonstrate an average Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of approximately 0.005% for amplitude and phase calibration under direction-independent array errors, and an average RMSE of 0.25% for position calibration.

articleTitle: A Proposal for Vegetation Detection on Distribution Networks using Deep Learning for Satellite Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Electricity interruptions caused by vegetation close to the distribution network are common in several energy distributors that use overhead networks. The growth of vegetation in contact with the grid can result in temporary or permanent faults, interrupting the supply of electrical energy, impacting indicators and system reliability. This work aims to develop a system for detecting trees that are close to the distribution network, so that preventive maintenance plans can be generated for tree pruning, avoiding contact with the network. To achieve this, computer vision and deep learning techniques are used to identify trees in satellite images taken from Google Earth. A YOLO model is trained with 105 images, 80 for training and 25 for validation, and cross-referenced with data referring to the georeferenced distribution network. A case study carried out in an urban setting is presented. The trees and the distribution network are identified in an image area. After this step, it is possible to extract the regions of the identified elements and find where the scenario is close to the network.

articleTitle: Radio Propagation Measurements and Analysis with Clutter Loss in Urban and Suburban Environments at 3.7 and 4.9 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This work aims to present and analyze clutter loss propagation measurements in 3.7 and 4.9 GHz, which are bands of interest for communications and next-generation networks. The clutter loss model has been widely debated in the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) due to its importance for coexistence studies, and its applicability for bands below 10 GHz in different environments, is currently being discussed. In this work, a narrowband signal measurements campaigns were carried out in dense urban and suburban environments in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, to calculate the path loss propagation with the aim of clutter loss characterization in these scenarios and evaluate the applicability of the clutter model and its limitations. This information will be useful for the regulatory process, including the evaluation of the prediction models used in Anatel’s coexistence studies.

articleTitle: Rigorous Green’s Function Derivation for Grounding Calculations Using the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The Method of Moments (MoM) is notoriously an efficient approach to simulating electrical grounding systems. Using this method, with the construction of a moment matrix, it is possible to calculate the potential at any point in space for a given excitation of the grounding mesh. By determining the potentials in the surface, the analysis of critical parameters in the design of grounding systems is enabled, such as touch voltage, step voltage and grounding resistance. This paper describes the mathematical development required to find a general solution for modeling grounding systems via MoM, using the Green’s function concept. As a final result, the use of the function in calculating the moment matrix is demonstrated in a simple simulation case: two parallel conductors buried in a uniform soil. Additionally, the advantages of the implemented solution over those presented in previous articles [1], [2] are highlighted. In this new solution, numerical integration is no longer required, making the code faster and numerically robust.

articleTitle: Brazilian Electromobility: A Brief Overview and Early Outcomes from an R&D Project
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This study examines the evolution of electromobility in Brazil over the past five years, focusing on historical trends, market growth, and the impact of political incentives. A comparative analysis situates Brazil’s progress within the global landscape of electromobility, highlighting the gradual expansion of the electric vehicle (EV) fleet and market share. Insights from a recent Research and Development (R&D) project, which implemented and monitored 11 EV fast-charging stations, reveal key patterns in station usage, energy consumption, and operational challenges. The findings underline significant progress, including increased EV adoption, improved charging infrastructure, and enhanced user confidence, while also identifying critical challenges such as station congestion, uneven infrastructure distribution, and the need for more targeted public policies. This dual perspective of achievements and barriers offers a comprehensive outlook, guiding policymakers and industry stakeholders in developing strategic actions to accelerate Brazil’s transition to sustainable transportation.

articleTitle: Cross-Protocol Repeater for Sigfox and LoRa Networks Using Cognitive Software Defined Radio Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has witnessed a rapid expansion, necessitating efficient communication technologies such as LoRa and Sigfox. In light of the crescent number of devices connected to Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks, it is necessary to manage multiple protocols, such as LoRa and Sigfox, for effective spectrum utilization. In this work, the reconfgurability of software defined radios explored to develop a cross-protocol repeater for LoRa and Sigfox protocols, enabling seamless integration between different devices. Experimental observations led to bit-error-ratios (BER) of less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, yielding satisfactory performance for most applications.

articleTitle: Power Quality Assessment of PFC Topologies Applied to Electric Vehicle Chargers Connected to Low-Voltage Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The interconnection of electric vehicle chargers without proper planning of electrical power grids can lead to power quality issues, such as an increase in harmonic pollution and a low power factoR, requiring countermeasures to mitigate these impacts. Hence, power factor correction circuits are usually designed for electric vehicles. In this context, the aim of this work is to evaluate three consolidated power factor correction topologies (capacitor dividers, power factor correction boost and Totem Pole), as well as an electric vehicle charger topology without power factor correction circuit implemented, focusing on the power quality aspect of the grid. Simulation results show that without the presence of a power factor correction circuit, high harmonic levels and a low power factor cor¬rection occur. Moreover, by implementing the passive correction circuit, the harmonic pollution is partially mitigated, but a low power factor is still present. On the other hand, active power factor correction topologies obtained the best performance for increasing the power factor. Particularly, the results show that the Totem Pole topology stands out, since the boost power factor correction topology resulted high harmonics pollution at high frequencies (i.e. supra-harmonics).

articleTitle: Evaluating the Influence of Phase-Locked Loops on the Response of Grid-Following Inverter-Based Resources to Interconnection Transmission Line Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of different Phase-Locked Loops (PLLs) on the fault response of a grid-following (GFL) Inverter-Based Resource (IBR) is evaluated. The analyzed IBR represents a wind power plant with rated power equal to 100 MVA, being composed of 50 turbines with 2 MVA each, whose controls follow the Brazilian grid code. Two PLL models are taken into account to conduct the proposed studies, which include the analysis of voltage and frequency estimated by each PLL, and currents injected into the IBR interconnection transmission line. The Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) PLL and the Quadrature Signal Generator-based Second-Order Generalized Integrator (QSG-SOGI) PLL are considered, assessing their influence under different transmission line fault scenarios. The obtained results indicate that the PLL can present severe instabilities during faults, which can be more or less critical depending on the fault type and on the PLL type. Indeed, the results reveal that different PLLs can result in distinct behaviors of currents injected into the interconnection line, raising the importance of knowing the PLL structures when studies on IBR fault responses are of interest.

articleTitle: A Controled Kalman Based Spherical Modal Expansion of a Measured Radiated Far Field
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This work presents a novel method for estimating mode coefficients in the spherical mode expansion of an antenna based on far-field radiation samples. The algorithm employs a mode-recursive strategy inspired by the Kalman Filter to produce high-quality, asymptotically unbiased estimators free from numerical artifacts. It also allows for controlled minimization of residual energy and covariance, enhancing accuracy and precision. The method effectiveness is validated through its application to a 260GHz Pillbox antenna, with results compared against standard batch methods.

articleTitle: Implementation of Adaptive Algorithms for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation in Satellite Communication with Large-Space Array
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm, for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems using a Uniform Planar Antenna (UPA) array at the ground station. The paper discusses about the subspace tracking techniques used in the algorithms for DOA estimation process, and simulations are performed to evaluate the accuracy of these algorithms in a real based satellite communication scenario, in which it novels for implementing a method of FDM (Frequency Division Multiplexing) for array element for mitigating grating lobe effects. The results demonstrate acceptable performance for estimation in this context, depending on direction of signal arrival.

articleTitle: Spectral Variation-Based Compression: A Case Study with Leakage Current Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This work presents a spectral variation-based compression method for leakage current signals from high-voltage insulators. This scheme is applied to real data acquired from sensors installed at Hub Sergipe. We propose the Spectral Variation Detection Algorithm (SVDA), adapted from the Spectral Variation Detection and Compression System (SVDCS) and implemented on a resource-constrained IoT device. The algorithm optimizes storage by leveraging the Hermitian symmetry property, enabling efficient frequency-domain compression. Using signals digitized at 7.68 kHz, the best compression ratio achieved with the default threshold was 38.7:1. This method provides a practical solution for compressing leakage current signals in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Power Control and Clustering for Terrestrial and Aerial Users in D-MIMO Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: While the majority of the D-MIMO studies consider dedicated networks serving only terrestrial users, this paper investigates the cluster formation and data power control problems for the uplink of D-MIMO networks that simultaneously serve terrestrial and aerial users. In this context, we formulate optimization models for mobile networks to improve three main areas: minimum and total spectral efficiency, as well as total energy efficiency, ensuring an all-around enhancement of network performance. Due to the combinatorial nature of the formulated non-linear programming problems, we solve these problems following a two-step procedure. The first stage employs a simple and suboptimal method for decentralized cluster formation, while the second stage advances to sophisticated centralized power control algorithms, utilizing strategies from convex optimization and fractional programming theories. In our analysis, we comprehensively examine the impact of aerial user mobility on optimization metrics, assessing the effectiveness of power control versus traditional solutions in scenarios involving mobility.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Sensitivity Analysis Methods Applied to Distributed Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The use of statistical techniques, such as stochastic processes, Monte Carlo simulations and analysis of variance (ANOVA), has been widely used in power system analysis and are essential tools for developing studies and models with high methodological rigor. Sensitivity analysis, on the other hand, is widely recognized for its importance in robust modeling and uncertainty assessment, and although it is receiving increasing attention, it is still underused. For this reason, this study aims to compare sensitivity analysis methods in the context of power systems, assessing their effectiveness. To this end, a methodology that determines the technical impacts of the insertion of photovoltaic distributed generation on a feeder was adapted to evaluate the effects of inverter, system and location factors on average voltage violations. The results show the superiority of the global sensitivity analysis, which, by using Monte Carlo simulations, associates uncertainties in the inputs with the outputs, revealing previously unknown correlations or confirming existing ones, such as the well-known influence of inverters' reactive power on bus voltages and its potential application in voltage control.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Hosting Capacity: An Approach Based on Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The growing integration of photovoltaic (PV) distributed generation (DG) presents challenges and opportunities for distribution networks, requiring a precise evaluation of the network’s Maximum Hosting Capacity (MHC). This study aims to determine the Maximum Hosting Capacity (MHC) of the EPRI ckt5 distribution system using optimization techniques based on the optimal power flow (OPF) approach, considering technical constraints such as voltage limits. The methodology for simulation was implemented in Python using OpenDSS. Two methods were applied: centralized allocation, which evaluates each bus individually, and distributed allocation, which considers simultaneous PV allocation across multiple buses. The results show an average MHC of 75.40 kW in the centralized approach, while the distributed approach resulted in a lower average of 35.84 kW, reflecting the impact of equitable resource allocation. The study highlights the trade-offs between maximizing technical capacity and promoting fair access to PV generation.

articleTitle: Detection of False Data Injection Attacks in Power Systems Using Deep Autoencoder with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The evolution of electrical power systems into smart grids has increased their efficiency but has also introduced new vulnerabilities, particularly in the form of cyber-attacks. One such threat is the False Data Injection (FDI) attack, which can bypass traditional Bad Data Detection (BDD) mechanisms, thereby posing significant risks to system security. Detecting such attacks is crucial to ensure the security and stability of power systems. In this paper, a self-supervised deep autoencoder model with an attention mechanism is applied to detect FDI attacks in power systems. Two datasets were used: one containing real measurements from an IEEE 14-bus system and another containing attack vectors. These datasets were randomly combined to form a compromised dataset. A model was then developed with the goal of distinguishing real measurements from attack vectors. The performance of the model was subsequently analyzed using appropriate metrics, which achieved a high detection rate with minimal false positives, demonstrating its robustness

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Inverter Failures on the Efficiency of Photovoltaic Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper assesses the impacts of failures in inverters on efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) generation systems. Six PV systems located in the northeastern region of Brazil are studied from January 2022 to July 2024, allowing the assessment of failure occurrence logs. In the proposed study, additional climatic data obtained from National Institute of Meteorology (INMET) system is taken into account, such as solar irradiation and temperature. By doing so, the expected PV generation system efficiency is validated and the impacts of inverter failures on their generation capacity are investigated. The obtained results show that some systems are more prone to issues due to inverter failures than others, particularly in response to grid availability and voltage quality. Furthermore, it is estimated that inverter failures can result in efficiency losses that can range from 2.55% to 14.67%. These results highlight the need for proactive solutions to detect inverter problems and for methodologies to enhance the PV generation capacity forecasting.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Different Techniques for UHF Signal Classification of Partial Discharges
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this article, a comparison of different machine learning techniques for the classification of UHF partial discharge signals is presented, namely: Artificial Neural Network, Support Vector Machine, and Fuzzy Logic. The database used consisted of signals obtained in the laboratory through a printed monopole antenna with a bandwidth between 319 MHz and 1.6 GHz, which captured signals from three test objects: oil cell, potential transformer, and ceramic insulator. After creating the database, various features were extracted from the signals, including statistical parameters of the signal in the time domain and its normalized autocorrelation function, as well as characteristics of the signals in the frequency domain. Subsequently, the features that best characterized the signals were selected using the Relief algorithm and then applied to the classification algorithms. From the obtained results, it was noted that the Support Vector Machine achieved the highest accuracy in classifying the defects, reaching 98.57%, followed by Artificial Neural Networks and Fuzzy Logic, with 97% and 83.33%, respectively.

articleTitle: Modeling Uncertainties in Electricity Consumption Using the Z-Score Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The pursuit of energy efficiency in power systems emphasizes the need to accurately model uncertainties in electricity consumption, which are inherently stochastic due to human behavior. Non-parametric methods offer precise representations but may become impractical when data is limited. Conversely, parametric methods, such as the Z-Score, provide more straightforward solutions by assuming a known distribution, although they may incompletely capture data variability. This study evaluates the applicability of the Z-Score for modeling consumption uncertainties by comparing it to equivalent percentiles using real-world data. Error metrics such as MAE, MSE, RMSE, and SMAPE are used to quantify the differences between the approaches. Although exact equivalence between Z-Scores and percentiles is uncommon, the results highlight that the parametric method provides accurate estimates in intermediate ranges, making it a viable option for modeling uncertainties in electricity consumption under data-limited scenarios.

articleTitle: Alternative Low Voltage Cable Model for Transient Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents an alternative model for low-voltage (LV) cables, which is implemented in the Alternative Transients Program (ATP/ATPDraw) to support transient studies. The presented modeling strategy combines the Bergeron approach to implement a frequency-independent line model, including low pass filters to emulate cable attenuation, and if necessary, transient responses of voltage and current sensors used to measure transients in field applications. A step generator is also modeled to emulate a cable step response laboratory assembly in the ATP/ATPDraw environment. To validate the developed model, laboratory tests with real 6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> LV cables with PVC insulation representing a two-conductor single-phase LV circuit are carried out. Comparisons between real and simulated circuits prove the accuracy of the developed model, highlighting its usefulness and revealing it as a promising model for transient studies in LV lines.

articleTitle: Metaheuristic Approach Hybridizing Variable Neighborhood Search and Genetic Algorithm to Size Hybrid Backup Systems for Power Outages
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybridization approach of metaheuristic techniques for sizing hybrid backup systems to supply essential loads during power outages. Two classic metaheuristic techniques were considered for this application, with contrasting search philosophies: the Genetic Algorithm and the Variable Neighborhood Search. The proposed method is analyzed through a case study for the maintenance of auxiliary services in a substation. The hybrid approach was compared with the pure metaheuristics that it is based on, observing the processing time and quality of the solution found. Finally, a statistical analysis was carried out to verify the performance of the techniques in a sequence of repetitions. The results obtained in this study suggest that although the hybridization proposal has a higher processing time than the other methods, it provided greater assertiveness in solving the problem.

articleTitle: CAN-Modes: In-vehicle datasets generation and analysis in different driving situations
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In-vehicle networks are responsible for safety-critical control applications, depending on data communication between electronic control units, and most are based on the CAN protocol. A huge amount of data is necessary for reliability, safety, and cybersecurity analysis in today's automotive solutions, especially to feed machine learning models. It is relevant to provide comprehensive datasets about CAN communication and different driving situations, which represents a lack in recent research because most public datasets are very limited. This paper addresses this problem by providing a set of CAN datasets collected in real cars and driving conditions, analyzed, and preprocessed for further research applications. The results present data collection and labeling, in three car brands, two data types (RAW and OBD pids), and they are available in recognized public sources.

articleTitle: Real-Time Co-Simulation of Voltage Control in Battery Energy Storage Systems for Distribution Networks with High Photovoltaic Penetration
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This article presents a real-time co-simulation framework for voltage control in distribution networks with high penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation, using Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The integration of PV generation can cause overvoltage issues, fluctuations, and reverse power flow. To mitigate these effects, the proposed solution combines active and reactive power control through BESS. The co-simulation, which integrates the OpenDSS and Typhoon HIL platforms, allows real-time monitoring and control of voltage levels. Reactive power control is performed through Volt-Var control, while active power control is based on the state of charge (SoC) of the BESS. Tests carried out on the IEEE 33-bus system, with PV generation and BESS, demonstrated that the proposed strategy is effective in maintaining voltage stability, mitigating overvoltages and undervoltages, and ensuring safe network operation. This study highlights the importance of using BESS to ensure stability in distribution networks with high penetration of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Proposal for Induction Motors Using IoT and Finite Elements Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Induction motors are susceptible to adverse conditions such as mechanical overload, voltage unbalance, mechanical vibrations, and short-circuits, which can lead to overheating and compromise their lifespan. An accurate analysis of thermal behavior is essential to prevent damage and optimize performance, especially under severe conditions. This work proposes a real-time remote thermal sensing technique using digital twins and the Internet of Things. The developed system performs thermal simulations based on the finite element method, executed in parallel with the motor in operation, capturing real-time data on current, voltage, humidity, and ambient temperature to feed the digital model. The system was experimentally validated in the laboratory, showing an average absolute error lower than 3.6% in the worst-case scenario. This technique enables continuous and remote simulation, providing a non-invasive and precise solution to enhance motor performance and prevent failures.

articleTitle: Automated Data Acquisition Method for a Legacy Intelligent Electronic Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of an automated data acquisition system designed to enhance relay testing for legacy Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) models with limited communication capabilities. The case study focuses on the MiCOM P443, a transmission line protection relay with only serial communication. The proposed method allows to capture fault location and classification data, automating the process previously managed manually through proprietary software. To do so, computer programs were developed, whose modular design facilitates the real-time data extraction via serial ports along with the translation of hexadecimal data packets, ensuring reliable and continuous fault event monitoring. Compared to traditional data acquisition manual methods, the proposed method drastically reduces data retrieval time and minimizes human intervention, contributing to more efficient testing procedures. The code for the algorithm presented in this paper is publicly available for replication, as well as for future work aiming to expand the data acquisition algorithm capabilities.

articleTitle: Dual Versus Dedicated Clustering in D-MIMO Networks With Aerial and Ground Users
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this work, the performance of distributed multiple-input and multiple-output networks simultaneously serving uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) and ground user equipments (GUEs) is evaluated considering dual and dedicated strategies of access points clusterization. In the dual approach, the two types of users can share the same access point array, while in the dedicated one an access point array can serve only one type of user. The schemes were implemented using the dynamic cooperation cluster (DCC) method and the k-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm based on the large scale coefficients. In the dedicated scheme, the access point array is up-tilted to benefit the served UAVs. The results show that, due to the restriction in cluster size of KNN, the DCC algorithm is better for the UAVs for both dual and dedicated schemes, specially with the up-tilted arrays. For the same reason, KNN works best for GUEs. Moreover, employing a dedicated KNN method for GUEs and the DCC method for UAVs along with up-tilted access point arrays in the same scenario provides the best results for both types of users.

articleTitle: Power Dispatch in Fast Charging Nanogrids: The Critical Role of Battery Degradation
publicationTitle: 2024 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The recent surge in electric vehicle (EV) adoption has introduced a dynamic landscape of challenges and opportunities in energy management for fast charging infrastructures. Efficiently harnessing renewable energy sources alongside battery storage is paramount to optimizing energy consumption and minimizing operational costs. Utilizing empirical data from an operational fast charging nanogrid, we developed an advanced mathematical model to evaluate the interplay between photovoltaic generation, grid integration, and battery storage. Our comprehensive analysis reveals that neglecting battery degradation costs significantly inflates total operational expenses. By incorporating degradation costs into the dispatch model, we demonstrate substantial improvements in both economic and operational efficiency. Validation with real-world data confirms significant cost reductions and performance enhancements when degradation costs are accounted for. This research highlights the imperative of integrating battery degradation considerations into energy management strategies, ensuring the sustainability and economic viability of EV charging infrastructures. The findings provide crucial insights for the future design and operation of sophisticated nanogrid systems, advocating for the broader adoption of renewable energy solutions in the expanding electric vehicle market.
